claims.text: 'One of the loopholes that we see in the law is that there is... no actual definitions or requirements for notification. Are there - what methods of notification did you observe? Like, when they say they notified Congress, how did they do that?'

'When there is a requirement for any agency or company to... notify Congress, do they contact the chairman of a committee? Do they get them on the phone specifically? Is this through an email to, hypothetically, a dead email box?'
'We have seen defense contractors abuse their contracts before through this Committee. I have seen it personally, and I have also seen the notification requirements to Congress abused.'

label: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
narrative: Ocasio-Cortez asked the most technically precise question of the 2023 hearing and it is the one that has aged best. Waived onto the subcommittee, she framed the committee as a whistleblower-protection body and then went at the funding mechanism rather than the phenomenon. Her line of questioning concerned Independent Research and Development - the mechanism by which defense contractors recover the cost of self-directed research from the government - and the statutory notification requirements attached to it. She told Grusch she had personally seen defense contractors abuse their contracts through this committee and seen congressional notification requirements abused, and identified the loophole: 'there are no actual definitions or requirements for notification.' She then pressed on the operational reality of that loophole - when an agency says it notified Congress, does it call the chairman of a committee, or is it 'an email to, hypothetically, a dead email box?' That is the question of whether the congressional notification that legally legitimates a waived unacknowledged program is a real event or a formality. She closed her round by asking all three witnesses, for the record, where she should look - 'titles, programs, departments, regions.' She attended the 12 January 2024 closed ICIG briefing.
